business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: People's Republic of China (China); target sub-entity Taiwan (TW) applies its separate municipal legal order under the Cross-Strait statutory framework

stage_2.competent_industrial_authority: 臺灣港務股份有限公司 (Taiwan International Ports Corporation, Ltd.; TIPC) - 港務管理處, supervised by 交通部 (Ministry of Transportation and Communications, MOTC)
stage_2.operating_license_title: 船舶貨物裝卸承攬業經營許可證 (Stevedoring Cargo Handling Contractor Operating License) under 商港法 (Commercial Port Law), Article 31, and 港區作業管理規定

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: 環境部 (Ministry of Environment; MOENV) - formerly 行政院環境保護署 (Environmental Protection Administration; EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Bulk terminal cargo handling operations involving dry bulk (e.g., coal, ore, cement) trigger Category B (第二類) 環境影響說明書 (Environmental Impact Statement) review where the new development area equals or exceeds 2 hectares, or Category C general registration control for existing operating facilities; construction subject to 開發行為應實施環境影響評估細目及範圍認定標準 (Development Actions EIA Detailed Items and Scope Standards), Items on 港灣開發工程. In all events, the operator must obtain 固定污染源設置及操作許可證 (Fixed Pollution Source Installation and Operation Permit) under 空氣污染防制法 for dust-generating bulk cargo handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Install bag filters/enclosure and comply with PM10 (dust) emission limits; wastewater discharge conforms to 放流水標準 (National Effluent Standards) under 水污染防治法: pH 6-9, chemical oxygen demand (COD) ≤ 100 mg/L, suspended solids (SS) ≤ 30 mg/L, grease ≤ 10 mg/L, oil ≤ 10 mg/L (for port-area discharges); fugitive dust opacity shall not exceed 20% per 空品區 ambient AAQS; rainwater runoff from cargo yards treated through oil-water separators and sediment basins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and its electronic tax portal (e-Tax Bureau / 电子税务局); in Taiwan jurisdiction, the competent authority is the National Taxation Bureau (財政部各地區國稅局) under the Ministry of Finance, with the integrated tax declaration portal (電子申報繳稅服務).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a WFOE established in mainland China, the foreign investor must first obtain a business license (营业执照) from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), after which the company must register for tax with the competent STA branch within 30 days using the Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC) as the tax identification number; the WFOE must complete taxpayer registration for corporate income tax, VAT, and other applicable taxes, and obtain the tax registration certificate data via the e-Tax Bureau. For Taiwan-related operability, if the entity maintains a Taiwan branch or fixed place of business, a separate Taiwan tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau is required, using the company's Taiwan Business Registration Number (統一編號).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not provide check-the-box elections; corporate income tax is levied at entity level on the WFOE. The WFOE may elect general VAT taxpayer status for input VAT crediting. Taiwan branch profits are subject to Taiwan entity-level taxation with a possible tax credit for Taiwan-sourced taxes against mainland CIT, subject to cross-strait tax rules and anti-avoidance limitations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (China Value-Added Tax) and Taiwan VAT/Business Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A person engaged in taxable supplies with annual business volume exceeding CNY 5,000,000 is generally required to register as a general VAT taxpayer; below that threshold, simplified taxpayer status applies at 3% collection rate, though port stevedoring services are taxable supplies and a WFOE will normally register as a general taxpayer to claim credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandatory digital e-invoicing is being phased in under the 'fully digitalized electronic invoice' (数电票) system; taxpayers must use the STA's e-invoice platform, submit invoice data in near-real-time through API or web interface, and obtain a unique invoice code for fiscal clearance. Taiwan operates the E-Invoice (電子發票) platform with mandatory Uniform Invoice issuance and cloud-based submission; no real-time government pre-clearance stamp is required, but invoices must be transmitted within 48 hours for cloud invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: China's export VAT zero-rating applies to exported goods; port stevedoring services supplied in China to non-resident carriers for international shipping or for goods in transit are generally zero-rated if the services are provided in connection with export and paid in foreign currency. Taiwan zero-rating applies to services rendered in Taiwan that are used or enjoyed outside Taiwan, and to services related to international transport.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (出口收汇核销单/银行收汇水单)
Sales contract and export invoice (外销合同/商业发票)
Customs declaration mark of physical export verification (海关出口货物报关单验讫记录)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export VAT zero-rating or refund claims are subject to severe penalties including confiscation of refunded tax, payment of late fees, a fine of up to 5 times the tax evaded under China's Tax Administration Law, potential loss of export tax rebate qualification, and criminal liability for tax fraud. Taiwan imposes penalties under the Tax Collection Act for sham transactions, including fines and imprisonment for fraudulent zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC); the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau, supervises banks and relevant financial institutions; the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Review Division administers applicable foreign investment registration and approval matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a generally liberalized foreign-exchange regime. The New Taiwan dollar is broadly convertible for ordinary trade, service, and other current-account transactions, subject to anti-money-laundering controls, documentary verification, bank reporting, and restrictions applicable to particular counterparties or transactions. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, capital injections, equity transfers, intercompany financing, guarantees, and certain securities transactions, may require prior approval, registration, reporting, or bank documentation depending on the investor, transaction type, amount, counterparty, and applicable nationality or cross-strait rules. A Taiwan operating company may generally remit dividends, interest, principal, service fees, royalties, and other permitted amounts offshore after satisfying corporate approvals, withholding-tax obligations, accounting support, bank review, and any required investment or foreign-exchange filings. The submitted data contains a jurisdictional inconsistency: the sovereign-country code is CN, while the jurisdiction is TW and the entity is described as a CN WFOE. This blueprint treats Taiwan as the operating jurisdiction and assumes that the entity is lawfully established or registered there. If the entity is instead a Mainland China WFOE, the People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange regime must be substituted, and Taiwan-specific conclusions must not be used.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan generally does not impose a universal statutory requirement that export proceeds be surrendered to the CBC or converted into New Taiwan dollars within a fixed period, and no general mandatory conversion ratio applies to ordinary export receipts. Exporters may ordinarily retain foreign-currency proceeds in approved foreign-currency accounts or convert them through authorized banks. Banks must verify the underlying commercial transaction, retain or obtain relevant customs, invoice, bill-of-lading, contract, and settlement evidence, and complete required foreign-exchange reporting. Proceeds involving restricted countries, sanctioned parties, unusual payment structures, related-party settlements, or cross-strait counterparties may be subject to enhanced review, licensing, reporting, or prohibition. The company should reconcile export receivables, customs declarations, bank credits, and invoices and maintain evidence supporting the business purpose and beneficial ownership of each receipt. If the actual entity is in Mainland China, export proceeds, foreign-currency retention, and conversion rules are materially different and must be assessed under SAFE rules, including applicable export-receipt verification and foreign-exchange settlement requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.regulatory_boundary: The company must not treat this dossier as a substitute for transaction-specific confirmation by a Taiwan authorized foreign-exchange bank and local counsel. Port operations may additionally involve customs, port authority, maritime, cargo-handling, sanctions, and trade-control requirements that affect account opening and payment screening.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment initiation and collection support; Low for replacing a Taiwan domestic bank account or independently holding regulated customer funds. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment service provider generally cannot provide unrestricted Taiwan deposit-taking, domestic payment, foreign-exchange, or escrow services without an applicable Taiwan license, approved local structure, or regulated-bank partnership. The company should use a Taiwan authorized bank as the principal account holder and limit any fintech provider to documented collection, payment orchestration, foreign-exchange execution, virtual-account, or reconciliation functions legally available to that provider. Offshore wallets must not be used to disguise capital contributions, export proceeds, related-party loans, payroll, customs payments, or port disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by every director is not universally mandated by statute, and banks may permit remote onboarding or use of notarized and legalized documents for low-complexity cases. In practice, a foreign-owned entity, a newly incorporated WFOE, a port-sector business, a China-linked ownership chain, a high-value foreign-currency account, or a request for trade finance and derivatives commonly triggers an in-person interview, video interview, authorized-signatory verification, beneficial-owner confirmation, and enhanced source-of-funds review. The bank determines the final requirement. Directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and finance officers should be prepared to attend remotely or in person and to explain the operating model, expected transaction corridors, cargo flows, counterparties, and treasury controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between CN sovereign metadata, TW jurisdiction, and the claimed WFOE legal form
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation or registration; articles of association; business registration; foreign-investment approval or registration; tax registration; written legal memorandum identifying the actual place of incorporation and governing law; board resolution confirming the account-opening jurisdiction; corrected KYC master data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership is obscured through offshore holding companies, nominee shareholders, trusts, or layered affiliates
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership chart to the natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; registers of members and directors; passports and residential evidence; trust deeds and protector information where applicable; corporate registry extracts; shareholder declarations; independent-source confirmation; explanation of each intermediate entity and economic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-Taiwan cross-strait nexus, restricted counterparties, or unexplained fund flows between Mainland China and Taiwan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty list with nationality and ownership; sanctions and restricted-party screening record; transaction-purpose memorandum; applicable approvals or filings; contracts, invoices, customs records, and bills of lading; bank payment route; confirmation that no prohibited financial institution, restricted person, or prohibited service is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Port terminal and stevedoring activity lacks evidence of statutory licensing, concession rights, or port-authority approval
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Port operating license; terminal concession or lease; stevedoring authorization; environmental and safety approvals; customs and maritime registrations; port-authority contracts; insurance certificates; business plan showing the precise services and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected turnover, currency mix, or payment corridors are inconsistent with the stated business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial forecast; monthly cash-flow model; customer and supplier concentration report; signed contracts; tariff schedule; vessel and cargo-volume assumptions; expected monthly inbound and outbound payment matrix; explanation of seasonal peaks and related-party transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection appears to be a loan, trade payment, or third-party remittance rather than paid-in equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution; capital subscription agreement; investment registration or approval; audited source-of-funds evidence; remitter ownership proof; bank remittance instruction stating the correct investment purpose; capitalization schedule; prohibition on third-party remitters unless expressly documented and accepted by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, offshore wallets, virtual assets, cash, or unrelated third-party accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy requiring company-account use; account-control matrix; payment approval workflow; explanation and remediation of historical exceptions; bank statements; source-of-funds records; written no-cash and no-personal-account policy; employee training evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade characteristics, including dual-use cargo, sanctions exposure, unusual routing, shell-company customers, or cash-intensive port services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due-diligence files; end-use and end-user certificates; cargo classification; bills of lading; customs declarations; vessel and ownership screening; sanctions screening logs; beneficial-owner certificates; escalation and transaction-monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, accounting, or foreign-exchange support for dividends, royalties, interest, service fees, or intercompany charges
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing analysis; invoices; withholding-tax computations and payment receipts; board approvals; audited accounts; arm's-length benchmarking; evidence of services performed; foreign-exchange purpose documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for derivatives, large credit facilities, or foreign-currency limits without demonstrated hedging need
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; exposure register; hedge accounting policy; forecast cash flows; underlying contracts; risk limits; authorized dealer confirmations; derivative suitability and appropriateness records; evidence that derivatives are not being used for speculative trading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital through a Taiwan authorized foreign-exchange bank into the company's designated capital or foreign-investment account. The remittance instruction should identify the investor, beneficiary, equity subscription purpose, currency, amount, and legal entity name exactly as registered. Avoid third-party remitters, netting against unrelated invoices, cash deposits, and mixed-purpose wires. Before remittance, obtain any required foreign-investment approval or registration and provide the bank with the subscription agreement, shareholder resolution, ownership and source-of-funds evidence, constitutional documents, and applicable regulatory filings. After receipt, the bank should issue or retain the foreign-exchange and inward-remittance evidence required for capitalization and registration. Transfer funds from the capital account to the operating account only under the bank's approved procedure and after satisfaction of capitalization conditions. For intercompany loans, guarantees, or shareholder advances, use a separate documented instrument, identify the correct loan purpose, satisfy applicable borrowing and foreign-exchange rules, and do not record debt as equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_operating_receipts: Receive customer, port-authority, shipping-line, and agent payments into the company's designated New Taiwan dollar or foreign-currency account. Use invoices, service contracts, cargo records, port tariffs, bills of lading, and settlement references that reconcile the payment to the underlying service. For export-related or cross-border services, retain customs and commercial evidence and ensure that the bank's foreign-exchange purpose classification matches the transaction. Apply customer receipts to the correct legal entity and do not pool funds with affiliates without a documented cash-pooling arrangement and legal, tax, and regulatory review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Taiwan authorized-bank clearing rails for vessel, cargo, equipment, fuel, insurance, customs, port, and supplier payments. SWIFT MT103 or the bank's current ISO 20022 cross-border payment equivalent is appropriate for standard wires, subject to complete originator, beneficiary, purpose, invoice, and sanctions data. Commercial letters of credit may be used for qualifying equipment, cargo, and supplier transactions; the bank should issue or advise the LC only against approved credit limits, verified trade documents, and a clearly identified underlying transaction. Documentary collections, open-account payments, and supplier finance may be used where commercially appropriate. Each payment file should contain the purchase order, contract, invoice, shipping or service evidence, customs documents where relevant, tax treatment, beneficiary ownership screening, and dual approval. Do not use payment references that misdescribe capital, loans, dividends, or trade receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_profit_and_intercompany_remitta: Remit dividends only after legally required financial statements, distributable-profit determination, shareholder approval, withholding-tax review, and any required investment or bank documentation. Remit interest, royalties, management fees, and service fees only under written agreements supported by evidence of performance, transfer-pricing analysis, invoices, withholding-tax compliance, and applicable foreign-exchange reporting. Maintain a remittance register showing gross amount, currency, beneficiary, purpose, tax withheld, approval date, bank reference, and supporting documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_pooling_and_sweeping: Maintain separate ledgers and bank accounts for paid-in capital, operating cash, restricted funds, customer or authority funds, payroll, taxes, and hedging collateral where applicable. A zero-balancing or notional cash pool with offshore or affiliate accounts requires review of Taiwan corporate, foreign-exchange, tax, transfer-pricing, financial-regulatory, and cross-strait restrictions. Use written cash-pooling agreements, arm's-length interest, documented borrowing limits, daily reconciliation, entity-level consent, and clear beneficial ownership. Do not sweep customer or restricted funds into a parent account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.clearing_architecture: Primary rails should be Taiwan domestic clearing for New Taiwan dollar payroll, taxes, utilities, port charges, and local suppliers; authorized-bank foreign-currency accounts for USD, EUR, JPY, and other approved currencies; SWIFT or equivalent bank messaging for international wires; commercial LC or documentary collection for higher-risk trade; and bank-host-to-host or secure API connectivity for controlled bulk payments. Implement payment sanctions screening, maker-checker approval, beneficiary whitelisting, transaction limits, callback verification for changes, daily bank reconciliation, and independent review of rejected or repaired payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Taiwan bank, supported by identified or forecast commercial exposures and documented maturity, notional, currency, and settlement terms
Non-deliverable forwards only where offered and permitted by the authorized bank and applicable Taiwan rules, with a documented underlying exposure and no speculative purpose
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-tenor management, subject to bank documentation, credit limits, and genuine funding needs
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or asset-liability matching, subject to suitability review, approved documentation, collateral terms, and board-approved risk limits
Currency options and option structures where the bank confirms legal availability, suitability, disclosure, accounting, and non-speculative use
Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, foreign-currency operating accounts, contractual currency clauses, and exposure netting where legally and commercially valid
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.hedging_controls: Adopt a board-approved treasury policy defining eligible instruments, approved counterparties, exposure thresholds, tenor limits, collateral and margin rules, segregation of duties, valuation, hedge designation, exception escalation, and reporting. Maintain an exposure register covering receivables, payables, debt, capital commitments, forecast port revenues, equipment purchases, and intercompany balances. Execute derivatives only with authorized dealers after confirming underlying exposure, ISDA or equivalent documentation, suitability, confirmation, valuation, and accounting treatment. Prohibit leveraged or speculative derivatives unless separately authorized and legally permissible.
operational_control_matrix: Daily cash position by bank, account, currency, and legal entity
Rolling thirteen-week liquidity forecast with base, downside, and severe-stress scenarios
Daily reconciliation of bank statements, payment files, trade receivables, trade payables, and foreign-exchange settlements
Dual authorization for new beneficiaries, capital movements, intercompany transfers, dividends, and derivatives
Monthly review of foreign-exchange exposures, hedge effectiveness, counterparty limits, and unhedged balances
Quarterly review of licenses, bank mandates, beneficial ownership, sanctions controls, and authorized signatories
Annual independent testing of AML, payment controls, cash pooling, derivative governance, and disaster-recovery procedures
principal_risk_flags: Misclassification of the entity as a China WFOE when the operating jurisdiction is Taiwan
Cross-strait remittances without documented approval, licensing, or restricted-party analysis
Third-party capital injections or payments that obscure the true investor or beneficiary
Failure to distinguish equity, shareholder loans, trade receipts, dividends, and service-fee remittances
Use of offshore fintech wallets as substitutes for regulated Taiwan bank accounts
Unlicensed port operations or payments inconsistent with the stated stevedoring scope
Speculative foreign-exchange derivatives, unsupported forecast hedges, or excessive maturity mismatches
Pooling of restricted customer, port-authority, payroll, or tax funds with general corporate liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Central Company Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year end (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects company to administrative fine of NTD 10,000–50,000 (approx. USD 330–1,670) plus daily penalty; repeated non-compliance may lead to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by deadline triggers a fine of NTD 3,000 (approx. USD 100); underpayment assessed at 3x deficiency plus interest, and criminal exposure for fraudulent omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in loss of foreign investment protection, forfeiture of dividend remittance rights, and a fine of NTD 60,000–250,000 (approx. USD 2,000–8,330).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit if paid-in capital exceeds NTD 30 million (approx. USD 1 million) OR annual revenue exceeds NTD 30 million; additionally, all foreign-owned enterprises approved under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals must file audited financial statements regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (T-IFRS) endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); local private enterprises with no public interest obligations may apply the Company Act and Business Entity Accounting Act standards (local GAAP).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require an annual UBO declaration for private limited companies; however, any change in shareholding must be recorded in the company's shareholder register within 15 days and reported to MOEA for registration. The annual shareholders' meeting serves to ratify the shareholder list and share transfer ledger entries.
